annotations.text:
Today's /professor.

Six equal-weight buttons, three cards that describe permissions rather than showing anything, and a fourth card repeating a button that is already on the page. Nothing here tells you what is waiting on you.

Direction A — Overview.

The hub answers "what needs me?" before it lists tools. The pipeline strip makes the two separate gates visible — you approve content, then you release it — which is the thing this app models and the old page never showed. One primary action per card; tools demoted to a list.

Counts and names are sample data, not real numbers.

The same shell on a sub-page: breadcrumb, section nav, one page title, one status badge.

Every professor page inherits it, so the navigation never disappears mid-task the way it does today (each page's only way back is a "Back" link to the home page).

Direction B — Console.

Same tokens, different bet: a persistent left rail and a triage inbox, so reviewing IS the landing state instead of somewhere you navigate to. Faster for working through a backlog; gives up the at-a-glance pipeline overview, and the rail costs 248px on every page.

Pick one direction — I would not ship both.
